candidates.title: Organize app security signals before install

demandEvidence.chore: A store operator wants to check whether a Shopify app has an official security review mark before installing it.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I’d appreciate any guidance on how to verify an app’s security before installing it in my store.

experimentPlan.output: A one-page evidence checklist that records an app listing’s stated security signals and unanswered verification questions without declaring the app safe.
inputs: Operator-copied official badge or certification text
experimentPlan.trigger: A store operator is considering a Shopify app and supplies its public listing information.
steps: Record the listing URL and the operator-copied claims.
Separate claims attributed to the listing from independently verified details.
Mark each checklist field as present, absent from supplied materials, or unverified.
Draft questions for the operator to confirm with the vendor or platform.
Have the operator review the record; do not issue a security verdict.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Given a fictional listing with mixed supplied claims, confirm the checklist preserves attribution and labels unknown fields without converting them into a safety rating.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator supplies public materials, independently checks any official status, and makes the install decision; the proposed aid cannot certify security.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference supports official badge lookup or security verification.
The source does not show how often operators face this decision or whether they would pay for help.

ease.reason: The proposed worksheet can organize operator-supplied public listing details; no source documents a security-verification method or reliable badge lookup.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: Shopify store operators may value a pre-install review aid, but this single question proves no payment or buyer demand.

feasibility.reason: A four-week evidence organizer is bounded, but no source supports deciding whether an app is actually secure; it must avoid a verdict.

autonomy.reason: A template can flag missing evidence from entered details; a person must inspect sources and decide whether to install.

evidence.reason: The retained post asks about official app-security marks and pre-install verification; frequency and actual risk examples are absent.

candidates.reason: Scored as a bounded evidence-organizing experiment, but excluded below threshold because no verified method or buyer corroboration is supplied.

candidates.title: Outline agent checkpoint recovery steps

demandEvidence.chore: Agent developers need to write checkpointing and recovery logic and handle idempotency for their agents.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: But devs need to write checkpointers, recovery logic, and deal with idempotency by theirselves.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewed recovery-design worksheet for one interrupted synthetic agent run, listing checkpoint state, retry assumptions and idempotency questions.
experimentPlan.trigger: An agent developer provides one fictional or sanitized interrupted run for design review.
steps: Summarize the supplied run and identify the last known completed step.
List state that the operator says must survive a restart.
Mark every external side effect and whether it may repeat.
Draft checkpoint and retry questions without prescribing executable recovery.
Have an engineer review the assumptions and record unresolved decisions.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fictional run with one repeated side effect, check that the worksheet flags the repeat risk and leaves the recovery choice unresolved for engineer review.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An engineer defines state, authorizes retries, and validates idempotency; the worksheet neither runs agents nor changes production systems.
unverified: No implementation reference documents checkpoint storage, recovery execution or idempotent operations.
Useful state and retry behavior vary by agent and are not supplied in the post.
Frequency of this work and willingness to pay are unknown.

ease.reason: A beginner can turn operator-supplied failure notes into a structured design worksheet, but no implementation evidence supports agent recovery behavior.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: teams building agent workflows may pay for recovery planning, but this post shows no purchase intent or validated buyer.

feasibility.reason: A four-week worksheet for one synthetic interrupted run is bounded; correct checkpoint and idempotency rules depend on the agent design.

autonomy.reason: The proposed worksheet can produce repeatable questions, while an engineer must choose safe state and validate any recovery behavior.

evidence.reason: The post explicitly names checkpointing, recovery logic and idempotency work, but gives no examples, frequency, constraints or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Fresh assessment scores the explicit chores anew; the scoped proposal remains below threshold because implementation behavior, buyer demand and recurrence are unverified.

candidates.title: Prepare an app discoverability review brief

demandEvidence.chore: An app maker wants to figure out how to get people to find their apps.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: because I had no idea how to get people to find my own apps.

experimentPlan.output: A review brief listing possible app-store listing improvements and unanswered discoverability questions from operator-supplied app details.
experimentPlan.trigger: An app maker supplies one app listing and asks for ways to improve how people find it.
steps: Record the supplied listing text and intended audience.
Extract claims and terms already present in the listing.
Draft a short set of clarity and audience-match questions.
Suggest wording experiments as hypotheses, not proven ranking factors.
Have the maker review every suggestion before changing the listing.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: With fictional listing details, verify that the brief separates observed listing text from suggestions and does not claim a change will improve downloads.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The maker supplies accurate listing materials, chooses any edits and checks outcomes; the brief cannot establish app-store ranking behavior or guarantee discovery.
unverified: No implementation reference supports keyword research, app-store ranking analysis or download attribution.
The source gives no app category, listing details, audience, frequency or corroboration.
Buyer willingness to pay and useful measurable outcome are unknown.

ease.reason: A beginner could organize supplied listing details, but no source supports reliable keyword or ranking analysis.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: app makers may pay for discoverability help, but this single maker statement proves no market or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week review brief is bounded, but useful recommendations and any ranking effect cannot be verified from the supplied source.

autonomy.reason: The brief can repeat text review, while the maker must choose edits and assess outcomes; no ranking or attribution capability is documented.

evidence.reason: The excerpt states difficulty getting people to find the maker’s apps, but gives no concrete listing task, constraints, frequency or corroboration.

candidates.reason: The fresh excerpt supports a limited discoverability task, so it receives a scoped assessment; the plan remains below threshold because the actual app/listing workflow, implementation support and repeat demand are unknown.

steps.message: Assessed all five sealed discussion assignments. The video-editing and research-session excerpts describe products without a bounded chore and were excluded. App security, app discoverability and agent recovery received scoped five-criterion assessments, but each remains below the six-point threshold; no post is proposed.
